verdict_word: Loss wider, revenue edged up, bookings lumpy
takeaways: Revenue of $4.5 million grew 21% from a year ago and edged past the roughly $4.3 million analysts expected, but the adjusted loss of $0.13 a share was wider than the $0.10 expected (Investing.com, Seeking Alpha).
Remaining performance obligations were $38.3 million, up 1,221% from a year ago, per the company release.
GAAP gross margin was 52.9%, down from 71.4% a year earlier (Investing.com summary of the release).
Q3 bookings alone were weak at $1.9 million, down 19%, even as nine-month bookings rose 611% to $37.4 million.
The company also cited a Department of Commerce funding arrangement of up to $100 million, a DOCOMO production application and a new CGI partnership.
verdict: D-Wave beat on revenue, missed on the loss, and its bookings did a roller coaster impression: huge for the year, a shrug for the quarter. Quantum investors are used to holding their breath, so no change there.
